verses.text: From Paul, a prisoner for Christ Jesus, and from our brother Timothy. To Philemon, our dear friend who works with us,
to our dear sister Apphia, to Archippus who fights alongside us, and to the church that meets in your home.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God when I mention you in my prayers,
because I hear about your love for all God's people, and your faith in the Lord Jesus.
I pray that as you share your faith with others, it will work powerfully, as you come to know every good thing we have in Christ Jesus.
Your love has given me great joy and comfort, my brother, because you have cheered the hearts of God's people.
So in Christ I could be bold and order you to do what you ought to do.
But because of love, I would rather ask you. I, Paul, am now an old man, and a prisoner for Christ Jesus too.
I am asking you for my son Onesimus. He became my son in the faith while I was in chains.
Once he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
I am sending him back to you. Welcome him, because he is very dear to my heart.
I would have liked to keep him with me, so that he could help me in your place while I am in chains for the Good News.
But I did not want to do anything without your agreement. I wanted any kindness you show to be something you choose to do, not something you are forced to do.
Maybe the reason he was away from you for a short time was so that you could have him back for ever,
no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a dear brother. He is very dear to me, and even dearer to you, both as a person and as a brother in the Lord.
So if you think of me as your partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
If he has done you any wrong or owes you anything, charge it to me.
I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand: I will pay it back. And I will not even mention that you owe me your very self.
Yes, my brother, let me have this joy from you in the Lord. Cheer my heart in Christ.
I am sure you will obey, so I am writing to you. I know you will do even more than I ask.
And one more thing: get a guest room ready for me, because I hope God will answer your prayers and let me come back to you.
Epaphras, who is in prison with me for Christ Jesus, greets you.
So do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, who work with me.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
